promise_text: Proposal: pooling raises expected value (stake s wins 2s w.p. s/(s+1)). If all 4 points go to one player who stakes 4, expected return is 6.4 vs 4. Send your 1 point to agent_1; I stake all and split the winnings evenly back (~1.6 EV each vs 1). I'll post results. | Staked 4: WON 8. Sent 2 each to agent_2/3/4 as promised. Others still have unused games: pool again! Everyone (I'll add my 2) sends to agent_2, who stakes 8 (wins 16 w.p. 8/9) and splits 4 each. I'm sending my 2 to agent_2 now. | Great teamwork. agent_2: stake 8, send 4 each to agent_1/3/4. Then next pool to agent_3 (I'll send my 4), stake 16, split 8 each; then agent_4 last. | Sent my 4 to agent_3 (now 16). agent_3: stake 16, send 8 each to agent_1/2/4. Then all pool to agent_4 for the final stake.

agent_2: Sent my 1 to agent_1. Agree pooling is +EV (1.6 each vs 1). agent_3, agent_4: join in. agent_1, please stake the full pool and send back each contributor's equal share on a win. | agent_2: Thanks agent_1, honored! Second pool: agent_3 send me 2 (and agent_4 your 1 if you want). I'll stake the whole pool next turn and on a win return 2x each contribution (agent_3 gets 4, agent_4 gets 2). Pool of 5 wins with prob 5/6. | agent_2: Staked 7, WON 14. Returned 4 to agent_1, 4 to agent_3, 2 to agent_4; I keep 4. agent_3 and agent_4 haven't played yet—you could pool again. Happy to vote end when you're done. | agent_2: Sent my 4 to agent_3 for pool #3 (pool now 14, win 14/15). agent_3: on a win return 8 to me, 8 to agent_1, 4 to agent_4. Then agent_4 runs pool #4. | agent_2: Sent my 8 to agent_4 for pool #4 (pool 28, win 28/29). agent_4: on a win return 16 each to agent_1, agent_2, agent_3; you keep 8. Then we all vote end.

Proposal: pooling beats solo. Solo stake 1 = EV 1. Pool 4 in one agent, stake 4: wins 8 w.p. 4/5. Send your 1 pt to agent_1; I stake 4 and, if win, send 2 back to each of you (EV 1.6 each vs 1 solo). I'll commit publicly to redistribute. | Staked 4 and WON 8. Sent 2 to each of agent_2, 3, 4 as promised. All of you still have your own play left; a further pool could go higher (e.g. 6 pooled in one of you → stake 6, win prob 6/7). Happy to coordinate or vote end. | Joined — sent 2 to agent_2. agent_2: stake all 8, and on a win send 4 back to each of us as committed. | Sent 4 to agent_3. agent_3: stake all 16, on win return 8 to each of us. Then agent_4 pools last. | Sent 8 to agent_4. agent_4: stake all 32, on win return 16 each to agent_1, agent_2, agent_3 as everyone before you did. Then we all vote end. | Great teamwork — 16 each. Voting end.

Proposal: pooling beats solo play. Stake 1 has EV 1; stake 4 wins 8 w.p. 4/5. Everyone transfer your 1 point to agent_1; I stake 4 and, if I win, send 2 back to each of you (EV 1.6 each vs 1). I'll honor it publicly. | Won! 4->8. Following the chain: sent all 8 to agent_2. agent_2 stake 8, pass all to agent_3, then agent_4 stakes all and splits equally among the 4 of us. Let's honor it. | Great teamwork, everyone honored it. 16 each. Voting to end.

Proposal: pooling beats playing alone. Stake 1 = EV 1, but stake 4 wins 8 w.p. 4/5 (EV 6.4). Everyone send your 1 pt to agent_1; I stake all 4 and if it wins I send 2 back to each of you (EV 1.6 each vs 1.0). I'll keep my word—reputation is all we have here. | Stake 4 WON (8). Sent 2 to each of agent_2, agent_3, agent_4 as promised. Note: you each still have your own unplayed game—you could pool again (e.g., 6 to one of you, stake 6 wins 12 w.p. 6/7). Otherwise, vote end. | Joining: sent my 2 to agent_2. agent_2 now stakes 8 (wins 16 w.p. 8/9, better odds for everyone). If win: 4 each back to agent_1, agent_3, agent_4; agent_2 keeps 4. Then all vote end. | In—sent 4 to agent_3. On record: agent_3 stakes 16 (once agent_2 sends too); if win (32), 8 back each to agent_1, agent_2, agent_4. Then agent_4's final pool. | In—sent 8 to agent_4. On record: agent_4 stakes 32; if win (64), 16 back each to agent_1, agent_2, agent_3, agent_4 keeps 16. Then all vote end. Great teamwork everyone.

Proposal: pooling raises EV. Everyone send your 1 point to agent_1. I stake all 4 in round 2: 80% chance of 8 points, then I send 2 back to each of you. Your EV 1.6 vs 1 by holding. I'll report and pay back promptly. | Staked 4 and WON 8. Paid 2 back to each of agent_2, agent_3, agent_4 as promised. Everyone now has 2. You each still have your own play left; you can pool again if you want (e.g. send to one of you, stake 6 for 6/7 odds of 12). | Sent my 2 to agent_2. A2: stake 8, on win pay 4 back to each of A1, A3, A4. Then continue chain with A3, A4 same way. | Sent my 4 to agent_3. A3: stake 16, pay 8 to each of A1, A2, A4 on win. Then A4 final pool. | Sent my 8 to agent_4. A4: stake 32, pay 16 to each of A1, A2, A3 on win, as everyone before you did. Then we all vote to end. | All four pools won and everyone paid back. 16 each. Thanks all, voting to end.

Proposal: pooling raises EV (stake s wins 2s w.p. s/(s+1)). If all send 1 pt to one player, stake 4 wins 8 w.p. 80% (EV 6.4 vs 4). I'll volunteer as pooler and return 2 to each contributor on win. Or happy to send mine to another pooler.

Agreed. Sent my 1 point to agent_1. agent_1: please stake the full pool once all are in, then send 2 back to each of us on a win. agent_3, agent_4: join, it's +60% EV for everyone. | Thanks agent_1, paid as promised! agent_3: same trick again? Send your 2 to me, I stake 4 (80% to win 8) and send you 4 back on a win. EV 3.2 each vs 2.67 solo. agent_4 is welcome to add theirs too (stake 5, I return 2 for their 1). | Staked 7, WON 14. Paid out as agreed: 4 to agent_1, 4 to agent_3, 2 to agent_4, kept 4. agent_3 and agent_4 still haven't played, so another pool is possible if you want one. | In: sent my 4 to agent_3. agent_3, please stake all 14 and send me 8 on a win. Then agent_4 runs the final pool. | In for the final pool: sent my 8 to agent_4. agent_4, please stake all and send me 16 on a win. Then we all vote end.

Proposal: pooling beats solo play. Stake s wins 2s w.p. s/(s+1); EV of stake 4 = 6.4 vs 4 held. Send your 1 pt to agent_1, I stake all 4, and if I win (80%) I send 2 back to each of you (8 split evenly). Everyone's EV 1.6 > 1. I'll post every step. | Staked 4, WON 8. Sent 2 each to agent_2, agent_3, agent_4 as promised. Everyone holds 2. Note: you each still have your own play unused — stake 2 has EV 2.67 > 2 if you want it. Or vote end. | agent_1: Joined — sent 2 to agent_2. agent_2, please stake all 8 and on a win send 4 each to agent_1, agent_3, agent_4 as promised. | agent_1: Joined — sent 4 to agent_3. agent_3, stake all 16 once agent_2 joins, send 8 each to agent_1, agent_2, agent_4. Then agent_4 hosts final pool. | agent_1: Joined — sent 8 to agent_4. agent_4, once agent_2 joins stake all 32, send 16 each to agent_1, agent_2, agent_3, then we all vote end. | agent_1: Thanks all — everyone honored every promise. All games played, all hold 16. Voting end.

Pooling raises win probability for everyone: send me your 1 and I'll stake the combined pot next round. If all 4 pool and win, payout is 8: I'll distribute 2 to each participant. A solo stake wins only 50%; pooled stake 4 wins 80%. | Confirmed: all four contribute 1; I stake 4 only after all contributions arrive. On a win, each gets 2 (I send 2 each to agents 2, 3, 4 and keep 2); on a loss, all get 0. Agents 2 and 3 can transfer now; agent_4 follows.

Pooling all 4 points before playing gives an 80% chance of 8 points, versus separate coin flips. Send your point to me this round; I'll wait to stake the pooled balance until round 2, then distribute winnings equally among contributors. | Confirmed: if all four contribute 1 and the four-point stake wins, each contributor gets 2 points. I'll wait until round 3 to play so all contributions can arrive this round. We can then consider a second pooled game with an unplayed agent.

Pooling raises each point's expected return: send me your 1, I'll stake the combined 4 next round (80% win vs 50% solo). On a win I'll return 2 to each contributor, keeping 2 myself. All get expected 1.6 instead of 1; no need to play separately.

Pooling raises win odds: send your 1 point to me; with all 4 I'll stake 4 (80% chance of 8), then distribute 2 each on success. Even pooling 2 gives 2/3 chance of doubling. I'll wait until next round to allow transfers.

Pooling raises expected returns: if you each transfer your 1 to me, I can stake 4 (80% chance of 8). On a win, proposed split is 2 points each; on a loss, 0. That's 1.6 expected each versus 1 from solo play. I'll wait this round for pooling.

Pooling improves expected returns: send me your 1 before I play next round. I'll stake the combined pool and, on a win, return 2 per contributed point (keeping 2 for my own). With all 4, each gets 2 with 80% probability vs 50% solo. | Agreed: relay the full winnings through agents 2 → 3 → 4, then split equally among all four. Agent_2, please add your 1 to me this round; I'll play the full 4 next turn. This maximizes each game's odds and gives everyone equal expected returns.

Pooling raises expected returns: send me your 1 point and I'll stake the combined pool next turn, then return 2 per contributed point if it wins (0 if it loses). With all 4 pooled, each gets 2 with 80% probability instead of a 50% solo chance.

Pooling raises win odds: send your 1 to me before I play. With all 4 pooled, win chance is 80%; if we win I'll send 2 to each contributor (2 each including me). Please leave games unused so we can discuss follow-on pooling.

Proposal: staking 1 is EV-neutral, but bigger stakes have +EV (stake s: EV gain s(s-1)/(s+1)). If all send their 1 pt to me, I stake 4: 80% chance of 8, and I send 2 back to each of you. Your EV: 1.6 vs 1. I commit to redistributing. | Won! Staked 4, got 8, sent 2 to each of agent_2/3/4 as promised. Everyone has 2 now. You haven't played yet: staking all 2 is +EV (2/3 chance of 4). Another pool to one of you would be even better. I'm done playing. | In. Sent my 2 to agent_2. agent_2: stake all 8, and on a win send 4 back to each of agent_1, agent_3, agent_4. Thanks! | In. Sent 4 to agent_3. agent_3: stake all 16, on win send 8 each to agent_1/2/4. Then agent_4 runs the final pool. Great teamwork. | In. Sent 8 to agent_4. agent_4: stake all 32 once agent_2's 8 arrives, and on win send 16 each to agent_1, agent_2, agent_3 — everyone has honored so far. Then we all vote end. | Perfect run — 16 each. Thanks all! Voting end.

Proposal: pooling beats solo play. Stake 1 wins w.p. 1/2 (EV 1). Stake 4 wins w.p. 4/5 -> 8 pts. Everyone send 1 pt to agent_1; I stake 4 and if it wins I send 2 back to each of you (EV 1.6 each vs 1 solo). I'll post results publicly. | Staked 4: WON, got 8. Sent 2 to each of agent_2, agent_3, agent_4 as promised. You each still have your own unplayed game — could repeat pooling (e.g. pool 6 to one of you). Happy to end anytime. | In — sent 2 to agent_2. Terms: agent_2 stakes all 8; on win sends 4 back to each of agent_1, agent_3, agent_4. | In — sent 4 to agent_3. Terms: agent_3 stakes all 16; on win sends 8 back to each of agent_1, agent_2, agent_4. Then agent_4's final pool. | In — sent 8 to agent_4. Terms: agent_4 stakes all 32; on win sends 16 to each of agent_1, agent_2, agent_3. Everyone's honored so far — let's finish clean, then all vote end. | Thanks all — 16 each, every deal honored. Voting end.

Proposal: pooling beats solo play. Solo stake 1 = EV 1. Pool 4 into one agent, stake 4: 80% chance of 8 → split 2 each (EV 1.6 each). Send your 1 point to agent_1; I stake all and send 2 back to each of you on a win. Sequential plays could do even better. | Staked 4, WON → 8. Sent all 8 to agent_2 per the chain. A2 stake 8 → pass to A3 → A4. Final holder splits evenly. Thanks for the trust!

Proposal: pooling raises expected value (stake s wins 2s w.p. s/(s+1)). Chain: everyone sends 1 to agent_1; I stake 4 -> 8, send all to agent_2, who stakes 8->16, sends to agent_3 ->32, to agent_4 ->64, then split equally (16 each). ~65% success vs 1 each now. | Won: 4->8. Sent all 8 to agent_2 as agreed. Your turn agent_2!

Proposal: pooling beats solo play. Stake s wins with prob s/(s+1), so bigger stakes have better odds. If all 3 of you send me 1 point, I stake 4 (80% chance to get 8) and send 2 back to each of you. Expected value per agent is 1.6, versus 1.0 playing solo. I commit to paying out. | Staked 4 and WON, got 8. Paid 2 each to agent_2, agent_3, agent_4 as promised. You three haven't played yet, so you could pool again: all 4 of us send 2 to agent_2, who stakes 8 (8/9 chance to get 16) and pays 4 to each. I'm in if agent_2 commits to paying out. | In: sent 2 to agent_2. agent_2, stake all 8 and pay 4 to each of us on a win. After that agent_3/agent_4 can run the next pool and I'll join again. | In: sent 4 to agent_3. agent_3, stake all 16 and pay 8 each on a win. Then agent_4 runs the final pool and I'll join. | In: sent 8 to agent_4. agent_4, stake all 32 and pay 16 each to agent_1, agent_2, agent_3 on a win. After that everyone has played, so let's vote to end.

Proposal: stake EV is 2s²/(s+1), so pooling raises expected value. If all send 1pt to agent_1, I stake 4: win prob 4/5, payout 8. I will then send 2 back to each of you (even split). Solo stake 1 is only EV 1. Join?

Proposal: pooling beats solo play (stake 1 has EV 1; stake 4 wins 8 with prob 4/5). Send your 1 pt to agent_1. I'll stake 4, and if I win I send 2 to each of you (EV 1.6 each vs 1 solo). I'll post my results openly. If someone else would rather be the pool, fine too. | Staked 4, WON 8. Sent all 8 to agent_2 per the chain. agent_2: stake 8, pass to agent_3, then agent_4, who splits equally at the end.

We can improve expected returns by pooling all 4 points for one stake (80% chance of 8 vs four separate fair flips). Send your 1 to me; I'll stake the pooled balance next turn and, on success, send 2 back to each contributor. | All four points remain available. I'll wait through this round so everyone can join the original pool; agent_2, you can contribute now, followed by 3 and 4. On a successful 4-point stake, each contributor receives 2; on failure all stakes are lost.

Pooling improves odds: if you each send me 1, I can stake 4 (80% win). On a win I propose returning 2 to each contributor, keeping 2; each expects 1.6 vs 1 solo. I'll wait until next round to play so everyone can contribute. | Confirmed: on a successful pooled stake I'll promptly transfer 2 points to each agent who contributed 1. I'll wait through all your turns this round and stake next round, allowing all three to join.

Pooling raises expected returns: if all send me 1, I can stake 4 (80% chance of 8) and distribute 2 to each on success. Solo staking only wins 50%. I’ll wait until next round to allow contributions; please pool rather than play separately. | Confirmed: with all 4 points pooled, I’ll stake 4 and, on success, immediately send 2 each to agents 2, 3, and 4, retaining 2. No forced further pooling; everyone can decide independently afterward. Please send your 1 this round; I’ll play next turn.

Pooling raises win probability: send your 1 point to me and I'll stake the combined pool next round. On a win I'll return 2 points per contributed point, leaving each contributor doubled; with all 4 points pooled, success probability is 80%. | Confirmed: if all three contribute 1 point, I will stake the full 4 next turn and, on a win, transfer 2 points each to agents 2, 3, and 4. Everyone has now indicated willingness; please send contributions this round so we can proceed.

Let's pool for better odds: send me 1 each and I'll stake 4 next round (80% win vs 50% solo). On success, split the 8 equally: 2 each. Then we can repeat with an unplayed agent to grow the pool further. | Won: 8 points. Returning 2 each as promised. Let's pool all 8 with agent_2 next, then rotate to agent_3 and agent_4; after the final successful game the pool would be 64, or 16 each.

Pooling raises win probability: transfer your 1 to me; if all 4 points arrive I'll stake 4 (80% win), then return 2 to each contributor on success. Each expects 1.6 vs 1 solo. If fewer contribute, I can stake the pool and split proceeds equally. | Thanks agent_4. Pool now has 2; agent_2 and agent_3, please join the established pool rather than fragment it. I'll wait this round for your transfers, then stake the full pool next turn and distribute 2 per contributor on success as proposed. | Won; all three contributors have received 2 as promised. I support agent_4's sequential pooling plan. Sending my 2 to agent_2 now: please pool all 8, stake next turn once funded, and pay 4 each on success. Then agent_3, then agent_4.

Pooling improves odds: send me your 1 point and I'll stake the pooled balance next turn. On a win I'll return 2 points to each contributor (keeping 2 if all join); loss returns 0. Each contributor's expected return rises from 1 to 1.6 with all four pooled.

Pooling raises expected total: a 4-point stake wins 8 with 80% probability, versus four coin flips. Send your point to me; I'll stake the pool next round. Proposed payout on a win: 2 points each. | Received agents 3 and 4's contributions; holding 3 points. Agent_2, please send your point this round so I can stake all 4 next turn as proposed.
